reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-3 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 21 rows and 4 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 2 rows and 10 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 14 rows and 17 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 18 rows and 11 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The fix visibly worked: unlike the stale review's generic 'Find the area of the rectangle.' stem, every current sample names the tile arrangement explicitly ('covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in N rows and M columns'), matching 'illustrate ... using square tile units' directly.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Rows/columns vary widely across the 7 seeds (2x10 up to 21x4 and 14x17), giving genuine numeric diversity rather than one repeated grid shape being re-skinned.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentence structure is a single short imperative clause naming rows and columns, well within grade-3 quarter-1 reading demand and free of extraneous clauses.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: I recomputed 21x4=84, 14x17=238, 18x11=198 and all match, but every sample is the identical rows-times-columns prose template, so the variant space doesn't yet include a version paired with an actual drawn tile grid image.

competency_alignment.rationale: The task stays on illustrating area via unit tiles rather than drifting into perimeter or the formula-naming lc that follows it later in this same quarter's sequence.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: A 14x17 or 21x4 tile grid (238 and 84 tiles respectively) is large for a first hands-on 'illustrate with square tiles' activity; a grade-3 quarter-1 introduction to counting tiles would more plausibly stay under a 10x10 grid a child could visualize.
